items.prompt:
Read.

'Bats are amazing animals. They can fly.'

The topic is:
A) Bats
B) Flying only
C) Mammals in general

steps: Whole text is about bats. Key is A.

items.prompt:
The sentence that introduces the topic is the:
A) conclusion
B) topic sentence
C) caption

steps: Introduces the topic. Key is B.

items.prompt:
Which belongs in an informative text?
A) facts and details
B) made-up adventures
C) opinions only

Read.

'The sun is a star. It gives us light and heat.'

Which is a supporting FACT?
A) The sun is a star
B) The sun is the prettiest
C) I love the sun
items.answer: A) The sun is a star

steps: A true detail. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) The sun is a star

items.prompt:
A word like 'another' or 'also' is used to:
A) add another fact
B) start an opinion
C) end the text

steps: Linking words add facts. Key is A.

items.prompt:
In informative writing, related facts should be:
A) grouped together
B) scattered randomly
C) left out

steps: Group related facts. Key is A.

items.prompt:
Which is the BEST topic sentence for a report on penguins?
A) Penguins are interesting birds that cannot fly.
B) I saw a penguin once.
C) It was cold yesterday.
items.answer: A) Penguins are interesting birds that cannot fly.

steps: Names the topic clearly. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) Penguins are interesting birds that cannot fly.

items.prompt:
Read.

'Spiders have eight legs. They spin webs to catch food. Spiders are helpful because they eat pests.'

Which sentence is the CONCLUSION-style idea (sums up why spiders matter)?
A) Spiders have eight legs.
B) They spin webs.
C) Spiders are helpful because they eat pests.
items.answer: C) Spiders are helpful because they eat pests.

steps: Sums up their importance. Key is C.
solution.answer: C) Spiders are helpful because they eat pests.
